queue_items.claim: The front seam at MT 8:22|MT 8:23 (= web:Isa.8.22|web:Isa.9.1) rests on a thematic tonal turn after the row itself disqualifies the only formal marker standing at MT 8:23.
queue_items.grounds: The row argues "the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle", having shown that the verse-initial "כִּ֣י" (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) recurs verse-initially at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6). No ruled tier-1 signal - frame onset, speech formula, vocative, imperative onset or addressee shift - is named at oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1), and the tier-3 parashah layer records no mark at MT 8:22, so the front seam as written carries no byte-standing seam signal at all. A byte-anchored candidate the row leaves unused stands in that verse's own bytes: the temporal-contrast pair "כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן" ... "וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד" (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier).
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: re-argue the front seam from the temporal-contrast frame in oshb:Isa.8.23's (= web:Isa.9.1's) own bytes, or drop confidence from medium to medium_low given that the span carries MT 9:5-6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7), a registered expected-low-confidence region. No span change proposed.

queue_items.claim: The rationale's closing rear-seam warrant contradicts the concession the same field makes about the same span.
queue_items.grounds: The field concedes "the unit is read as one sustained declaration, not because no fresh subject or addressee arises - both do", naming "הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ" (oshb:Isa.9.1 = web:Isa.9.2, byte tier) as the fresh nominal subject and "הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי" (oshb:Isa.9.2 = web:Isa.9.3, byte tier) as the turn to second person. It then closes "No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence, so the throne clause stays inside this unit." As written the two cannot both stand. The rear seam does not fall with it - the fresh declarative subject "דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י" (oshb:Isa.9.7 = web:Isa.9.8, byte tier) and the tier-3 SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) both hold - so this is a defective warrant rather than a boundary defect.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: scope the closing sentence explicitly (e.g. no further subject or addressee marker reopens after the birth clause at oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6) or delete it and rest the rear seam on the fresh declarative subject at oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8). No span change.

queue_items.claim: The closing splice and its paired gloss render different clauses of the same verse, and two further splice/gloss extents in the field do not match.
queue_items.grounds: The closing splice is the doubled ketiv/qere token pair "לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה" (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier), which WEB renders “Of the increase of his government”; the gloss actually paired with it is “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6), which renders a different clause of the same verse, "קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת" (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier). Two further mismatches: the six-token opening splice "כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒" (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) is glossed with the whole of web:Isa.9.1 through “Galilee of the nations.”; and the throne-name splice (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier) is glossed “His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (web:Isa.9.6 = oshb:Isa.9.5), which also renders "וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ" (oshb:Isa.9.5 = web:Isa.9.6, byte tier), outside the splice. The doubled-token engagement itself is correct - both staged forms are quoted and the medial final mem is correctly called letter bytes plus ketiv/qere apparatus, not a special-letter seg.
queue_items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: pair the doubled-token splice with WEB's own rendering of it, and re-cut the other two glosses to their splice extents. No span change.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens where the scene turns from darkened lands into light, at כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (oshb:Isa.8.23, byte tier), rendered “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.” (web:Isa.9.1) = oshb:Isa.8.23; the causal particle opening that verse recurs verse-initially inside the span at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6), so the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle. A fresh nominal subject then opens the following verse, הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.2, and the address turns second person at הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי (oshb:Isa.9.2, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.3, continued by הַחִתֹּ֖תָ (oshb:Isa.9.3, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.4; the unit is read as one sustained declaration, not because no fresh subject or addressee arises — both do — but because the chain of causal ki-clauses that follows (כִּ֣י אֶת עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ, oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4; כִּ֤י כָל סְאוֹן֙, oshb:Isa.9.4 = web:Isa.9.5) restates the same reason as the opening light and the multiplied joy, before the birth clause returns to third person, כִּי יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.6, without a further break in the argument. The throne-naming clause reads פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִי עַ֖ד שַׂר שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier), rendered “His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (web:Isa.9.6 = oshb:Isa.9.5); an OSHB exegesis note sits at this same verse (oshb:Isa.9.5), single-witness apparatus only, never text bytes, and is disclosed rather than argued as content. The unit closes at the government-increase clause, which the letter bytes stage as a doubled ketiv/qere token pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה (oshb:Isa.9.6, byte tier) — the ketiv form carries a final mem in medial position; the quote engages both staged forms, not one alone — rendered “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6). No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence, so the throne clause stays inside this unit.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the light-dawning announcement from the throne-naming and its government clause is rejected because the chain of coordinated ki-clauses keeps both halves inside one argument for the nation's joy.
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: A Masoretic setumah break follows oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7), tier-3 single-witness corroboration only, for a close already argued from the ki-chain and the fresh subject at web:Isa.9.8; it is never treated as the driver. A ketiv/qere note also sits at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3), inside this unit's own span; it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading. The medial final-mem in the doubled token is letter bytes plus ketiv/qere apparatus, not a special-letter seg of any size. The referent of the throne names (a court style exalting a Davidic king, versus a fuller messianic reading) is not settled by this boundary decision and is held open.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh conditional clause opens the row on an explicit second-person plural addressee against the first-person testimony closing at web:Isa.8.18, "הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י" (oshb:Isa.8.18, byte tier): "וְכִֽי יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם דִּרְשׁ֤וּ אֶל הָאֹבוֹת֙ וְאֶל הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים הַֽמְצַפְצְפִ֖ים וְהַמַּהְגִּ֑ים הֲלוֹא עַם֙ אֶל אֱלֹהָ֣יו יִדְרֹ֔שׁ בְּעַ֥ד הַחַיִּ֖ים אֶל הַמֵּתִֽים" (oshb:Isa.8.19, byte tier), matching “When they tell you, “Consult with those who have familiar spirits and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter,” shouldn’t a people consult with their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?” (web:Isa.8.19), the shift from “I” to “you” (plural) marking the front seam rather than the change in topic alone. The warning runs through the teaching-and-testimony appeal to its close, "וְאֶל אֶ֖רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט וְהִנֵּ֨ה צָרָ֤ה וַחֲשֵׁכָה֙ מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה וַאֲפֵלָ֖ה מְנֻדָּֽח" (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier), matching “then look to the earth and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick darkness.” (web:Isa.8.22), where the tonal reversal opening at oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) -- from the gloom just announced to a light-turning that begins the next unit's own frame -- closes this row's warning on its own terms.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative reads web:Isa.8.19-Isa.8.22 as still part of the preceding testimony unit (web:Isa.8.11-Isa.8.18) rather than a fresh row, but the shift from first-person prophetic resolve to a conditional warning about mediums argues a fresh topic onset.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: mediums-and-darkness close of the Immanuel-narrative arc
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: REAR-SEAM DISCLOSURE (zone-A edge): the row's rear boundary sits immediately before web:Isa.9.1 (= oshb:Isa.8.23), the Zebulun/Naphtali line that opens the following poem's turn from darkness to light; the tonal reversal is disclosed as an external continuity signal against the gloom announced at web:Isa.8.22, not adopted as evidence for extending this row past web:Isa.8.22. For disclosure discipline, the WLC parashah layer places a setumah at oshb:Isa.8.18 (single-witness, Prophets tier-3) alongside this unit without functioning as its cause. A word-level consonantal-skeleton echo straddles this seam: the sealed-testimony pair "צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה" (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier) and "לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה" (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier) share the same two nouns reversed; the pair's controlling object is word-level consonantal skeleton (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, MT 8:16 and MT 8:20). At byte tier neither testimony-noun form recurs elsewhere -- the absolute "תְּעוּדָ֑ה" is byte-unique to MT 8:16 (sweep: 1 verse) and the prefixed "וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה" is byte-unique to MT 8:20 (sweep: 1 verse) -- and the five-verse digit sometimes carried for the companion noun, "תּוֹרָ֖ה", is a skeleton-substring sweep (MT 2:3, 8:16, 8:20, 42:21, 51:4) whose own byte-tier count is 2 (MT 8:16, MT 42:21). A symmetric skeleton-tier echo sits on the seam an alternative bound would draw instead: "אֱלֹהָ֣יו" (oshb:Isa.8.19, byte tier) collates against "וּבֵאלֹהָ֖יו" (oshb:Isa.8.21, byte tier) at skeleton tier only. Neither echo is byte-identical, so neither outweighs a tier-1 signal at the seam it crosses, and moving the cut to MT 8:20|8:21 would only relocate this same skeleton-tier cohesion rather than remove it; both echoes are disclosed here rather than treated as grounds to relocate the boundary.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh declarative sentence with a new grammatical subject opens the unit: דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְנָפַ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.9.7, byte tier), “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.” (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7); Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria stand in apposition to the subject of the third-person plural verb that follows, וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.9.8, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.9 — an appositional expansion of that subject, not an addressed object — and the shift from the preceding unit's royal house is a shift of the oracle's target rather than of addressee: no second-person verb or suffix appears at any verse from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12). The unit closes at the refrain bracket אֲרָ֣ם מִקֶּ֗דֶם וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ מֵֽאָח֔וֹר וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל פֶּ֑ה בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.11, byte tier), “For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.12 = oshb:Isa.9.11).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this stanza through the next refrain occurrence is rejected because the following material renews the indictment with fresh content rather than continuing the same clause. A larger rival reads the whole judgment sequence as one continuous poem opening already at web:Isa.5.25 (the refrain recurs across five verses; sweep: 5 verses), with this stanza as a later movement rather than a fresh onset.
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark follows oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7), the verse immediately preceding this unit; tier-3, single-witness, disclosed even though the boundary is argued from the subject change rather than the mark. The closing refrain recurs byte-identically at five sites across the book (sweep: 5 verses), earliest at web:Isa.5.25, and on that basis a rival architecture reads the whole run from there as one continuous poem rather than granting this stanza its own bracket — disclosed rather than adopted.

queue_items.claim: The front-seam warrant describes the preceding stanzas as spoken to 'the nation addressed', but no second-person verb or suffix stands anywhere in oshb:Isa.9.7-Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.8-Isa.9.21); the nation there is a third-person target.
queue_items.grounds: Byte review of every verse of the preceding refrain-poem run: oshb:Isa.9.9 (= web:Isa.9.10) carries only third-person and first-person-plural forms, לְבֵנִ֥ים נָפָ֖לוּ וְגָזִ֣ית נִבְנֶ֑ה שִׁקְמִ֣ים גֻּדָּ֔עוּ; oshb:Isa.9.12 (= web:Isa.9.13) opens וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא שָׁ֖ב עַד (third person); oshb:Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.21) opens מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אֶת אֶפְרַ֗יִם וְאֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ (third person). The row shipped immediately before this one in the same stretch makes exactly this distinction load-bearing for its own seam, stating that no second-person verb or suffix appears from oshb:Isa.9.7 (= web:Isa.9.8) through oshb:Isa.9.11 (= web:Isa.9.12) and that the shift is 'of the oracle's target rather than of addressee' — a claim this audit re-verified true at byte tier. Two shipped neighbours therefore use 'addressee' incompatibly. The seam itself is unaffected: the ruled hoy woe-onset at oshb:Isa.10.1 carries it alone.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: re-cut 'the nation addressed in the preceding stanzas' to 'the nation targeted in the preceding stanzas' (or equivalent third-person wording); no span change.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A woe-onset opens the unit with a named class of offenders distinct from the nation addressed in the preceding stanzas: ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.10.1, byte tier), “Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees” (web:Isa.10.1). The unit nonetheless closes at the same refrain bracket as the three preceding stanzas: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.10.4, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.10.4).
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this stanza as an ordinary member of the surrounding woe-oracle series addressed to Assyria is rejected because its refrain reproduces the three prior stanzas' closing bytes (sweep: 3 verses) and its own target is the unnamed decree-writers, not Assyria. A rival architecture nonetheless reads the whole refrain-bracketed run as one poem rather than as this stanza's independent unit.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: woe oracle against unjust lawmakers, poem's fourth stanza
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: This unit carries both a formal woe-onset and the refrain-closed stanza pattern of the surrounding judgment poem; it is tagged for the onset it actually carries in its own bytes, with the refrain-poem membership disclosed as texture rather than folded into the type label. A Masoretic setumah mark precedes the unit at oshb:Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.21) and another closes it at oshb:Isa.10.4; both tier-3, single-witness. The refrain's five occurrences (sweep: 5 verses) start at web:Isa.5.25 and support a rival view that the whole run is one poem rather than four-plus independent stanzas, disclosed rather than adopted.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a fresh image continuing the same judgment voice, “For wickedness burns like a fire.” (web:Isa.9.18 = oshb:Isa.9.17), and closes at its own refrain occurrence: בְּכָל זֹאת֙ לֹא שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה (oshb:Isa.9.20, byte tier), “For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.” (web:Isa.9.21 = oshb:Isa.9.20).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this stanza into the woe-oracle that follows is rejected because the addressee shifts from the punished nation to a class of officials identified by participial description rather than by name, after the refrain closes here, not before. The refrain's five occurrences (sweep: 5 verses) start at web:Isa.5.25 and support a rival view that the entire sequence is one interrupted poem rather than four bracketed stanzas.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark falls at the unit's own closing verse, oshb:Isa.9.20 (= web:Isa.9.21), the same verse as the refrain; tier-3, single-witness corroboration for a close already argued from the bracket. Because the same byte-level refrain also closes web:Isa.5.25 and its other three sites (sweep: 5 verses), a rival architecture folds this stanza into one long poem beginning there rather than granting it an independent boundary — disclosed rather than adopted.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A new woe-onset addresses a wholly different subject — Assyria, not the decree-writers of the preceding unit: ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט (oshb:Isa.10.5, byte tier), “Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!” (web:Isa.10.5). The unit runs through Assyria's own boastful self-assessment and closes at the rhetorical question comparing Jerusalem to Samaria, הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי (oshb:Isa.10.11, byte tier), “shall I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?” (web:Isa.10.11), before a fresh temporal-response clause opens the next unit.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through the king's boast quotation that follows is rejected because a temporal-response clause opens a distinct divine reply rather than continuing Assyria's own self-description.
next_row.literature_type_guess: woe oracle against Assyria as unwitting instrument
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: A Masoretic setumah mark closes the preceding unit at oshb:Isa.10.4 and another closes this one at oshb:Isa.10.11; both tier-3, single-witness, disclosed though the boundary is argued from the addressee shift and the response clause that follows, not from the marks. The quotation formula כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (oshb:Isa.10.8, byte tier), “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8), separates the divine first-person speech of web:Isa.10.5-web:Isa.10.7 from the king's own quoted boast running web:Isa.10.8-web:Isa.10.11; the unit is held together across that internal frame because the boast is itself the content the divine word introduces, addressed to the same Assyrian figure in both halves, so the quotation is read as continuing the speech rather than opening a fresh unit. A ketiv/qere note also sits at web:Isa.10.6, staged as the doubled pair ולשימו וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ (oshb:Isa.10.6, byte tier); it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading, matching the practice already followed elsewhere.

queue_items.claim: The device_notes pairs the spliced quotation formula at oshb:Isa.10.8 with a curly-quoted WEB run that is disjoint from it — the gloss renders the clause that follows the formula, not the formula.
queue_items.grounds: The splice is כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר (oshb:Isa.10.8, collate: byte), and the run set beside it is “Aren’t all of my princes kings?” (web:Isa.10.8). web:Isa.10.8 opens “For he says,” and only then carries that boast clause — so the spliced two tokens are rendered by “For he says,” while the quoted English is the clause the formula introduces. Unlike the corpus's ordinary onset-splice-plus-fuller-gloss pattern, gloss and splice here do not overlap at all, so the pairing reads as though the Hebrew formula means the boast.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: re-cut the gloss to “For he says,” (web:Isa.10.8), or extend the splice to the boast clause it introduces; no span change.

This koh-amar is counted in the divine-frame class, not the royal-messenger class used elsewhere in the book's narrative material. The divine title stack opening this unit, אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier), is byte-identical to the stack closing the immediately preceding verse, אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.23, byte tier) — the book's only byte-tier occurrence of the stack (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier, 8 verses at skeleton tier) — and the seam still stands across it because the preceding verse carries the stack as the subject of a third-person judgment clause, while this verse's identical stack is the subject of the messenger verb אָמַ֞ר (oshb:Isa.10.24, byte tier) introducing a fresh, directly addressed assurance to Zion, so the recurrence alone does not carry the argument across the seam. This unit's own closing verse likewise opens with the in-that-day formula וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.27, byte tier), byte-identical to the formula that opens web:Isa.10.20, וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.10.20, byte tier), where it functions as a unit-opening driver (sweep: 5 verses at byte tier, 13 verses at skeleton tier); here the same formula stands unremarked inside the unit rather than opening it, so its boundary force is disclosed symmetrically rather than asserted selectively.
